findings.title: Title screen shows tanks, not cars
findings.where: Title screen, the two vehicles flanking the SMDUEL logo
findings.problem: The hero vehicles are clearly military tanks with prominent turrets, main guns, and heavy bolted armor. Every other screen (arena, road, city, constructor) uses the same small orange subcompact car sprite.
findings.why: First-impression mismatch. A player who sees tanks expects a tank game; when they load in and drive a sedan, the marketing and the product disagree, which makes the title feel like a placeholder or stock-art asset.
findings.fix: Replace the two vehicles with two stylised versions of the in-game car — e.g. a muscle car with a mounted gun on the left, an armored sedan with extra plates on the right — rendered at the same scale and lighting as the tanks so the hero shot still has weight.

findings.title: Constructor preview is an abstract outline, not the car
findings.where: Constructor screen, 'SUBCOMPACT - TOP VIEW' panel on the right
findings.problem: The preview is a blue rectangle with two plain inner squares. It does not show the chassis silhouette, does not indicate armour on any face, and shows no mounted weapons regardless of which row is selected on the left.
findings.why: This is the core RPG screen and its whole job is to show the player what they are building. Right now it looks like an empty placeholder; selecting 'Armor: Front' or 'Weapon 1' produces zero visual feedback on the car itself.
findings.fix: Draw the actual subcompact top-down silhouette (hood, cabin, trunk) and layer the equipped armour plates on each facing as colour-coded fills (front/rear/left/right/underbody). When a weapon is mounted on a row, render a small turret/mount icon on the appropriate edge and outline it when that row is highlighted.

findings.title: Radar reads as a broken disc, not an instrument
findings.where: Bottom-left HUD on arena and road screens
findings.problem: The radar is a dark green circle with only a faint static cone and a single crosshair dot. There is no rotating sweep line, no contact blips, and no obvious 'you are here' arrow tied to the car's heading.
findings.why: Players cannot tell whether the radar is functioning or whether the practice arena is simply empty. In a vehicular combat game the radar is supposed to be the primary situational-awareness tool; here it looks like an unfinished widget.
findings.fix: Add a rotating sweep arc with a brighter leading edge, draw a chevron at the centre pointing in the car's heading (replacing the generic crosshair), and render any nearby cars/NPCs as small dots whose colour reflects hostility (white for neutral, red for enemies).

findings.title: Armour condition panel shows identical empty boxes for every zone
findings.where: Top-right CONDITION panel on arena and road screens
findings.problem: All five armour facings (FRONT, REAR, LEFT, RIGHT, UNDERBODY) show the same dashed-outline empty box regardless of actual armour. There is no fill, no number, and no colour to distinguish an armoured face from a bare one. Only the separate 'Body armor × 0/3' line at the bottom conveys any numeric state, and only in red.
findings.why: Armour direction is the central combat mechanic — players must know which face is reinforced so they can angle incoming fire. Right now the HUD gives no readable answer; the eye has to go all the way down to the tiny red '0/3' to learn anything, and even then it is global, not per-facing.
findings.fix: Inside each FRONT/REAR/LEFT/RIGHT/UNDERBODY box, draw a horizontal fill bar whose width equals armour points and whose colour steps green → yellow → red as it depletes, and print the numeric value (e.g. '3') inside the box. Keep the empty/dashed look only when armour is genuinely zero.

findings.title: City buildings are undifferentiated grey boxes
findings.where: City screen, the structures scattered around the circular plaza
findings.problem: Every building is a near-identical flat grey block with a faint roof texture. None carry signage, colour, or a clear icon that tells the player what they do (garage, shop, mission board, arena entrance). The whole plaza is also mostly empty cracked ground.
findings.why: The city is the player's hub between runs — without readable landmarks they cannot navigate, cannot tell which building is interactive, and the screen reads as an empty test map rather than a lived-in place.
findings.fix: Give each building a distinct silhouette and a colour-coded floating icon above it (wrench for garage, dollar sign for shop, exclamation for mission, crossed-swords for arena). Add small ground props — parked wrecks, crates, lamp posts, NPCs — around the plaza edges so the space feels populated instead of empty.
